name: Genetic Immune Deficiency with Skin Involvement
aliases: Inherited Immune Deficiency with Dermatological Features

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Genetic Immune Deficiency Diagnostic Criteria with Skin Involvement

criteria.description: Recurrent, severe, or unusual infections indicative of immune dysfunction
Presence of chronic or recurrent skin lesions such as eczema, abscesses, or granulomas
Identification of pathogenic mutation in immune-related gene
Abnormal immunologic laboratory findings including lymphocyte subset abnormalities or immunoglobulin deficiencies
Positive family history of similar immune deficiency or skin disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent infections and cutaneous manifestations plus genetic confirmation of immune deficiency
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be supported by immunologic assays and family history but requires genetic confirmation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe recurrent infections with opportunistic pathogens

searchTerms: persistent yeast infections on skin and mucous membranes
nerve damage causing weakness or numbness

laboratory: Abnormal lymphocyte subset analysis (e.g., low T or B cells)
imaging: Chest X-ray showing recurrent pneumonia or bronchiectasis
CT scan revealing sinusitis or granulomatous lesions
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes involved in immune regulation (e.g., STAT3, DOCK8, WAS)
Confirmed mutation by sequencing or gene panel testing
other: Histopathology of skin lesions showing granulomas or lymphocytic infiltration
Flow cytometry demonstrating functional immune defects

distinguishingFeatures: Profound T and B cell deficiency
Early infancy onset with life-threatening infections
Absence of skin granulomas typical in genetic immune deficiency with skin involvement
Characteristic facial features and skeletal abnormalities
Eczema with recurrent skin abscesses but distinct genetic mutations

redFlags: Recurrent severe infections unresponsive to standard treatment
Chronic, non-healing skin ulcers or abscesses
Family history of early childhood deaths or immune deficiency
references: Notarangelo LD. Primary immunodeficiencies. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2010;125(2 Suppl 2):S182-94.

Picard C, Al-Herz W, Bousfiha A, et al. Primary Immunodeficiency Diseases: An Update on the Classification from the International Union of Immunological Societies Expert Committee for Primary Immunodeficiency. Front Immunol. 2015;6:54.
